newsitem.title: UK: Ghana opposes Anglo-Ashanti link - sources.
newsitem.headline: Ghana opposes Anglo-Ashanti link - sources.

text.p: Ghana will oppose any moves by South African mining giant Anglo American from forging a link with Ashanti Goldmines and will use its golden share to prevent a tie-up if necessary, industry sources said.
"They just wouldn't want any Anglo American involvement," said one source on Monday, who declined to be named.

The comments come shortly after a delegation of Anglo American senior executives, including chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson, visited Ghanaian president Jerry Rawlings. Both Anglo and Ghana confirmed there have been talks nearly two weeks ago, but they don't want to say what has been discussed.
Anglo has said in May it would be constructive to work together with Ashanti Goldfields, which is considered the showpiece of Ghana's reforming economy.
Thanks to Ashanti, which is listed in Accra, London and New York, gold is a booming sector in Ghana and one of the country's main export products.
Analysts earlier said that Anglo might want to use Ashanti as a vehicle to expand its gold interests in West Africa.
The link with the Ghanaian mine would likely have to established through British conglomerate Lonrho, which has a stake of about 30 percent in Ashanti.

Talks of Anglo looking for an indirect link with Ashanti emerged early this year when the South African firm gained a 7.3 stake in the British company. Speculation intensified after it acquired an option shortly afterwards to raise its holding to 25.7 percent.
Ghana has the power to effectively block shareholders gaining stakes in Ashanti of more than 20 percent and strip them of voting power if their stakes are against the public interest.
"Ashanti is a national asset of Ghana and the instant Anglo would become involved it would be Ashanti-Anglo American and that would be unacceptable to Ghana," a source said.
Another source said Ghana also objects to a link with Anglo because it feels this would harm Ashanti's good relationship with other African governments.
Ashanti operates in 10 African countries with the main exploration forays being in Ghana, Tanzania, Guinea, Senegal and Niger.
An Ashanti spokesman, meanwhile, said the Ghanaian firm would welcome Anglo American as it would any new shareholder.
